**把单词变成画面，让复习有迹可循。**
7,298 个雅思词条 · 原创插画 · 英美发音 · FSRS 间隔复习
[**立即体验 ↗**](https://0xlei.tech/words/)　 /　 [48 秒介绍](docs/assets/launch.mp4)　 /　 [下载词库](data/)　 /　 [English](README.en.md)

### 请我喝杯咖啡
这个项目开源，又免费，我自己投了很多钱和时间。觉得有用的话，请我喝杯咖啡吧。
     微信    支付宝   
---
词光是一款以插画和语境为核心的雅思背词应用。看画面理解词义，听发音建立联系，再用主动回忆和间隔复习巩固记忆。无需账号，学习进度保存在自己的设备上。
> **版本说明**：这个仓库提供词光的开源基础版及配套数据集。在线网站独立迭代，功能与仓库可能不同；仓库里的代码和内容分别遵循下方的 MIT / CC BY 4.0 授权。
[产品预览](#产品预览) · [学习方式](#学习方式) · [本地运行](#本地运行) · [开放数据](#开放数据) · [参与贡献](#参与贡献)
## 产品预览
### 一本可以听、可以练的单词图鉴
  每日计划，把注意力放在今天  插画、词义、发音，在一张词卡里  
 以上为仓库开源版的实际界面。页首为品牌概念插画。 
### 学过的词，汇成自己的星图
19 个话题组成词汇星图。拖动旋转、滚动缩放，点击星星打开词卡；学习状态用不同亮度呈现。采用 WebGL2 渲染，不支持的设备提供降级显示。
  看 48 秒宣传片  
[播放完整视频（含声音）](docs/assets/launch.mp4)
## 学习方式
| 环节 | 你会做什么 |
| :--- | :--- |
| **看见** | 每个词配一幅插画、中英释义、两条原创例句，以及搭配、词族和用法提示。 |
| **听见** | 切换英音、美音，听日常例句朗读；部分词条另含第二条例句录音。 |
| **想起** | 看义选词、看图补句、听音辨词、拼写，逐步练习主动回忆。 |
| **复习** | FSRS 根据学习记录安排复习，目标记忆率可调。只有首次作答计入正确率。 |
| **积累** | 星图展示学习进度；打字练习独立统计；支持导出和恢复本地进度。 |
**本地优先。** 无需注册；看过的词条与媒体可缓存供离线使用。换设备前，请先导出进度备份。
  听发音、例句与环境声样本  
拿 *abandon* 举例，点开就能听（在线播放）：
| | |
|---|---|
| 🇬🇧 英音 | [abandon /əˈbændən/](https://0xlei.tech/words/atlas/audio/uk/abandon.mp3) |
| 🇺🇸 美音 | [abandon /əˈbændən/](https://0xlei.tech/words/atlas/audio/us/abandon.mp3) |
| 📖 例句朗读 | [We had to abandon our car in the snow.](https://0xlei.tech/words/atlas/audio/ex/abandon.mp3) |
全部 7,298 个词都有英音、美音和例句朗读，还有 1,011 个重点词的第二条例句也配了朗读。
### 环境声与交互声音

| 🎵 **星空音乐** | [一段可无缝循环的原创配乐](https://0xlei.tech/words/sfx/amb-stars.mp3)，默认陪你背词 |

itens.descricao_en: Open-source gym & body-weight tracker, now in the App Store (iPhone + Apple Watch) and as an Android APK. Plan routines, log workouts, see which muscles are trained, import from Strong/Hevy/FitNotes. Self-host it or use it on the phone alone.
itens.readme:
[Website](https://opengym.ch) · [Live demo](https://opengym.ch/demo/) · [Roadmap](ROADMAP.md) · [Changelog](CHANGELOG.md)
## Why openGym
Most workout apps keep your data on their servers, push you towards a subscription, or vanish
when the company does. openGym runs on your own box, keeps your data in a folder you control, and
is yours to fork. It still behaves like a modern app: installable on the home screen, passkey
sign-in, works offline, syncs between your phone and your laptop.
No account on someone else's server, no subscription, no ads, no telemetry. One
`docker compose up` and it's running.
The [in-browser demo](https://opengym.ch/demo/) is the real app with example data,
if you want to try it before installing anything.
## Features
**Planning**
- A routine per weekday over a library of **over 5,600 exercises** with animated demos, searchable and
  browsable by muscle on a body map. Filter by the equipment you own.
- Four starter plans (Push/Pull/Legs, Upper/Lower, Full Body, 5×5) that load as ordinary,
  editable routines.
- Every session on the Plan page and today's on Home carries a tiny body map with the muscles it
  works lit up, so you know Leg Day is legs before you open it.
- Move a session to another day without touching the weekly plan. The week starts on Monday or
  Sunday, your choice.
- Or skip the weekdays altogether: a **rotation** (A, B, C, A, ...) where the next session is
  simply the next one you haven't done, however the week went.
- Supersets, warm-up sets, drop sets and rest-pause, timed exercises (planks, hangs, carries),
  cardio by time and speed, rest time per exercise, planned deloads.
- Your own exercises, with your own photo, GIF or short video. Location data is stripped on the
  device before upload.
**Training**
- Guided sessions: today's workout starts itself, weights are pre-filled from last time, a rest
  timer runs between sets, PRs are detected as you go. On a rest day it tells you when the next
  session is.
- A quiet workout screen: one menu per exercise, the set number as the set's own menu, card or
  list view. Switches in Settings bring the old button rows back if you liked them.
- Optional effort column as RIR or RPE, colour-coded, with a plain-language line per level.
- Plate math for barbell, EZ bar, trap bar and Smith machine, worked out from the plates you own.

itens.descricao_en: One-click character swap for videos: an open-source, local Higgsfield Genjutsu alternative built on ComfyUI and MiniMax H3, with FLUX.3 Klein relighting.
itens.readme:
# Openjutsu
An open-source, Genjutsu-style character and object swap for video. Drop a video and a character photo, press **Generate**, and the main person in the video is replaced by your character. Or change their hair or clothes, remove something, or put them somewhere else. The camera, cuts, motion and soundtrack stay. Everything runs on open weights on your own GPU: MiniMax H3 for the video, SAM 3.1 to track people, and Qwen3-VL 8B to describe the pictures and shots.
The app is a small Next.js front end over a ComfyUI workflow. It uses [`@comfyorg/sdk`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@comfyorg/sdk), following Comfy's [comfy-reshoot](https://github.com/Comfy-Org/comfy-reshoot) reference app.
https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/2d8d763a-1764-49a6-9116-d6d1be661ff6
| Advanced: several people, pick who becomes who | Object swap: paint where it goes |
| --- | --- |
|   |   |
| **From picture: a new look and place from one picture** | **Post-processing: fix faces** |
|   |   |
**From picture → Relight: new light in the same pass**
## First visit: visual describer
The welcome page lets you choose the vision-language model that describes pictures and video frames and writes prompts. Qwen3-VL 8B INT8 remains the default; Qwen3-VL 4B FP8 and Gemma 4 E2B INT8 are smaller alternatives. Install a compatible single-file model including its vision weights in `ComfyUI/models/text_encoders`, then press **Refresh models**. Other installed models can be selected if they support image/video input and text generation through ComfyUI's CLIPLoader and Generate Text nodes. Text-only models and files requiring a different loader are unsuitable.
Choose according to available VRAM and leave room for image/video context and working memory; file size is not a VRAM requirement, and H3 generation has separate memory needs. Your selection is saved in this browser and used for swaps, prompt descriptions and **Find people**. Reopen **Welcome & models** to change it, or use **Visual describer** under Model components. Alternative describers may change prompt quality and person matching. **Set up later** opens the editor; generation still checks the required files. The separate H3 text encoder remains unchanged.
## Modes
- **Simple motion transfer**: available. One character replaces the main person (the one who fills the most of the frame). Runs `workflows/simple.api.json`, exported from `H3 One-Click Single Swap (DMAD 6 step).json`.
- **Advanced motion transfer**: available. 1–4

itens.descricao_en: Sketch Material 3 Expressive screens in the browser and turn them into vibe-coding prompts.
itens.readme:
Sketch Material 3 Expressive screens in the browser, link them, tap through them, and copy a prompt for your AI coding tool. 
 Sketch the screens, tap through the flow, copy the prompt, and let your AI coding tool build the app. ( mp4 ) 
M3E Canvas is a free, open-source sketchpad for app screens made of real Material 3 Expressive parts. It runs entirely in your browser: no account, no server, nothing to install. What you sketch becomes a precise prompt that any AI coding tool that takes one, such as Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI or Cursor, can turn into a working app.
##   How it works
1. **Sketch** — Drag parts onto phone or desktop screens. They snap together and line up on a 4dp grid.
2. **Tap through** — Link parts to screens and press Preview to try the flow, transitions included.
3. **Copy the prompt** — The whole design becomes a short brief in your language. Paste it into your AI coding tool.
##   What's inside
  **Real M3 Expressive parts** — Buttons, FABs, bars, tabs, cards, lists, sheets, pickers, carousels, loading indicators and more, each with its own panel for text, style, size and what a tap does.
  **Screens and flow** — Phone and desktop screens, screens that scroll, taps and swipes that open other screens with the transition you pick, and arrows that show the whole flow.
  **Theme in one place** — Color, shape, type and motion: seven palettes or your own seed color, light and dark, three contrast levels, corner styles, fonts and the expressive spring motion.
  **Optional AI help** — Bring your own key to draft a design or write notes for you, or copy an instruction for a coding agent that replies with a share link. Keys never leave your browser.
  Everything it can do  
- **Parts** – buttons, icon buttons, FABs and extended FABs, FAB menus, split buttons, chips, top app bars, navigation bars and rails, floating toolbars, tabs, search bars, cards, list items, boxes, bottom sheets, dialogs, snackbars, text fields, dropdowns, switches, checkboxes, radio buttons, sliders, date and time pickers, text, images, carousels, camera and map placeholders, dividers, the shape-morphing loading indicator and wavy progress indicators. Every part has a panel for its text, style, size and alignment, and a trigger tab for what a tap does.

Shaders 
  WebGPU effects as components for React, Vue, Svelte, Solid and JavaScript
```bash
npm install shaders
```
## Table of Contents
1. [Why Shaders?](#why-shaders)

## Why Shaders?
-   **Real WebGPU, declarative API:** 200+ effects you drop in as components. Gradients, noise, glass, metal, light, distortions, transitions, blurs, cursor effects. Nest them, blend them, mask them.
-   **A design editor that writes your code:** design on an infinite canvas at [shaders.com](https://shaders.com), then export the exact component tree for your framework. Free.
-   **Every framework, one package:** first-class React, Vue, Svelte, Solid and JavaScript entries, with the same props everywhere.
-   **Production-ready:** TypeScript, extensively optimized, typed props with reactive updates, SSR safe. Used on thousands of websites by 16,000+ design engineers.
## 🧩 Components
Every effect is a component. ` ` renders the canvas; its children are layers, evaluated top to bottom and blended on the GPU.
### React
```jsx
import { Shader, LinearGradient, CursorTrail } from 'shaders/react'
```
Get started with [Shaders for React](https://shaders.com/react).
### Vue
```html
import { Shader, LinearGradient, CursorTrail } from 'shaders/vue'
```
Get started with [Shaders for Vue](https://shaders.com/vue).
### Svelte
```svelte
  import { Shader, LinearGradient, CursorTrail } from 'shaders/svelte'
```
Get started with [Shaders for Svelte](https://shaders.com/svelte).
### Solid
```tsx
import { Shader, LinearGradient, CursorTrail } from 'shaders/solid'
```
Get started with [Shaders for Solid](https://shaders.com/solid).
### JavaScript
```javascript
import { createShader } from 'shaders/js'
await createShader(document.getElementById('my-shader'), {
  components: [
    { type: 'LinearGradient', props: { colorA: '#0f172a', colorB: '#7c3aed' } },
    { type: 'CursorTrail' },
  ],
})
```
Get started with [Shaders for JavaScript](https://shaders.com/javascript).

itens.descricao_en: A Claude Code skill that reverse-engineers any animation frame by frame, then proves the copy moves the same.
itens.readme:
reanimate 
  Reverse-engineer animations you like. Build your own on top.  A Claude Code skill that works from a live site, a screen recording, an mp4, a gif or a Lottie file. 
  A short demo.  Watch the full video .  
A lot of good ideas start on someone else's site. Ask an agent to rebuild one from a link or a screenshot and it makes one pass, calls it done, and misses. It can't see the motion or tell how far off it is.
reanimate records the original, rebuilds it in your code, then records the copy the same way and compares the two. Each round shows what's still off, so the agent keeps going until the numbers match. You end up with a close starting point to make your own.
  Three cards from stripe.com. Top: the original. Bottom: the copy, filmed the same way.  
## Install
```sh
npx skills add NiazMorshed2007/reanimate -g
```
The [skills CLI](https://skills.sh) asks which agents to set up; add `-a claude-code` to skip the question. Then, in Claude Code, say what you want, where it is and where it should go:
```text
/reanimate the hero entrance on https://example.com, into components/Hero.tsx
/reanimate this loader, 0:03 to 0:05 of ~/Downloads/loader.mov
/reanimate the card hover in this gif, match it exactly
/reanimate the logo marquee from https://example.com, with our logos and pause on hover
```
Needs [Bun](https://bun.sh) 1.1 or later, on macOS or Linux (Windows is untested). The first run installs a static ffmpeg into the skill's folder and Playwright's Chromium into Playwright's usual cache, about 250 MB together. No API keys. Other agents that read `SKILL.md` can install it too, but it has only been tested with Claude Code.
## How it works
1. **Record.** It films the reference in a headless browser at a fixed viewport and frame rate: a video, numbered frames, every CSS and Web Animations API animation it finds, and the position of chosen elements on every frame. For canvas and WebGL it also traces the GPU calls (shaders, uniforms, draw calls, the three.js scene) on a virtual clock that makes every capture identical.
2. **Spec.** One row per element per property: start, duration, from → to, easing, stagger. A row with a "?" means the frames haven't been read yet.
3. **Build.** It writes the animation with what your project already uses: CSS, Framer Motion, GSAP, three.js.
4. **Verify.** It films the copy the same way, compares timing, easing and pixels, and makes side-by-side sheets.
5. **Repeat.** It fixes the biggest difference and films again, us

itens.descricao_en: A self-hosted job search and resume builder app that writes tailored resumes and cover letters from your profile.
itens.readme:
Dossier 
  Your job search, on your own server: one profile, a tailored resume and cover letter for every job, and every application tracked from draft to offer.
Dossier keeps your career history in one profile and turns it into a clean resume. For every job you apply to, it reads the posting, shows how you match, and drafts a tailored resume and cover letter that only use facts from your profile. You refine them in a chat, download them as PDFs and track each application from draft to offer.
It's for one person on a small server: one password, your data in your own PostgreSQL database (or a single SQLite file), and an AI model of your choice. That can be a local model through Ollama or LM Studio, so your profile and documents stay on your own hardware, or a hosted one (any OpenAI-compatible API, Anthropic or Mistral), which then receives what it writes from. [Privacy](https://github.com/AienTech/dossier/wiki/Privacy) says what goes where.
**Get started:** [run it on your computer](#run-it-on-your-computer) in a few minutes, or [self-host it](#self-hosting) on a server. The [installation guide](https://github.com/AienTech/dossier/wiki) covers every way: Docker with or without Compose, Node.js, a plain Ubuntu server, CapRover, Coolify and Dokploy.
**Or download the desktop app** for Windows or Linux from the [latest release](https://github.com/AienTech/dossier/releases/latest). It runs Dossier on your computer with nothing else to install, or opens a Dossier you host. See [Desktop app](https://github.com/AienTech/dossier/wiki/Desktop-app).
## Demo
 Recorded with the demo data (Jane Doe is made up) and a stand-in AI server that answers at once, played at 1.2× speed. With a real model, reading a posting and writing the documents takes from a few seconds to a few minutes. 
## Features
- **Profile:** basics, skills and languages, experience and volunteering, projects, education, certifications, publications and references, in the order you choose, with a strength meter that counts only what a profile needs. Projects (side, open-source, course or thesis work) show what you can do where your job titles don't yet. Certifications keep who issued them, their dates, credential ID and a link to verify them. Publications are cited in your own style, with bold and italics, and go on resumes word for word. Start it from an existing resume (PDF, Word or Markdown) if you like.
- **Base resume:** twelve themes and a theme builder, previewed live and printed to PDF on the se
